title: Microsoft Purview: information protection scanner data export for custom reporting
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents Custom Reporting in preview, including its SQL schema and PowerShell enablement, contrary to the briefing's central claim that there is nothing to configure. The default, database location, access controls and capacity guidance need correcting; the roadmap dates and existing scanner controls are accurately reported.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: No setting or command is documented for scanner data export, so there is nothing to configure.
claims.quote:
Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$true}
... This command enables the Custom Reporting feature for the entire scanner cluster. All nodes pick up the change on their next scan cycle. No service restart is required.
claims.fix: Keep controls[2].ui null, but set controls[2].api to powershell, call 'Set-ScannerConfiguration -FeatureSettings @{CustomReporting=$true}', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/purviewinformationprotection/set-scannerconfiguration?view=azureipps'. Replace its note with 'Preview; off by default. Enables reporting for the cluster on the next scan cycle. Set CustomReporting to $false to stop new writes; existing reporting data is retained.' Remove 'nothing to configure' from the summary and the no-command statements from the prose. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-feature-control and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; changes[0].note
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe scanner data export and its behaviour is known only from the roadmap.
claims.quote: This article describes the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner Custom Reporting feature (preview). Custom Reporting gives scanner administrators the data they need in the scanner cluster database to build their own reports against scan results
claims.fix: Replace the roadmap-only and no-Learn-documentation statements with 'Microsoft Learn documents Custom Reporting in preview for client and scanner version 3.2.89.0 or later, while the roadmap still lists In development with preview targeted for December CY2026 and general availability targeted for January CY2027.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting. Replace the summary with 'Custom Reporting (preview) stores scanner results in the cluster SQL database. It is off until an administrator enables it with PowerShell; review database access and capacity before opting in.'

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the export's SQL table names or columns.

### Additions to `dbo.ScannerFiles`
... ### New table: `dbo.MatchedClassificationAction`
... ### New table: `dbo.ScannedFilesArchive`
claims.fix: Replace the schema-absence statements with 'The preview documents additions to dbo.ScannerFiles and the new dbo.MatchedClassificationAction and dbo.ScannedFilesArchive tables, with column definitions on the Custom Reporting page.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting. Remove the question asking which tables and columns will hold the data.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether export data lives in the scanner database or elsewhere.
claims.quote: Custom Reporting moves file-state and SIT-match data into the scanner cluster database
claims.fix: Replace the unknown-location statements with 'Custom Reporting stores its reporting data in the scanner cluster database.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting and remove the database-location question.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented permissions governing access to the SQL reporting tables.
claims.quote: Database-level roles are database-wide in their permissions scope. ... Members of the db_datareader fixed database role can read all data from all user tables and views.
claims.fix: Replace the blanket absence claim with 'Reporting data is stored in the scanner cluster SQL database, where SQL Server database permissions govern access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting and https://learn.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/security/authentication-access/database-level-roles?view=sql-server-ver17. Remove the assertion that no access control can be identified; do not recommend granting broad database roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state that the four listed portal roles also govern the export.
claims.quote: Searched: "scanner" "Custom Reporting" "roles"; "scanner" "CustomReporting" "permissions" "read". Opened deploy-scanner-custom-reporting, deploy-scanner-feature-control and configure-install; no mapping of those four portal roles to PowerShell feature control.

claims.where: Scope: Not stated
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the scanner-cluster scope of export availability.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said how Custom Reporting affects scanner database upgrades.
claims.quote: Whether you're installing the scanner fresh or upgrading from any earlier version, the scanner deploys the full database schema (including the Custom Reporting tables and columns) on install or upgrade.
claims.fix: Replace the upgrade uncertainty with 'Installation or upgrade deploys the full Custom Reporting database schema; the reporting tables and columns remain unpopulated until Custom Reporting is enabled.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting. Remove the question asking whether the export changes the database upgrade step.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether export tables add to the scanner database's capacity needs.
claims.quote: When you turn on Custom Reporting, the scanner cluster database stores significantly more data: ... Building reports against the scanner cluster database also adds a read workload that runs alongside the scanner's operational reads and writes.
claims.fix: Replace the capacity gap with 'Enabling Custom Reporting significantly increases scanner cluster database storage and adds reporting reads alongside scanner operations.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/deploy-scanner-custom-reporting. Remove the question asking whether database size is affected; retain tenant-specific sizing as an administrator planning task.
